thread:
maya: heads-up from canary run — we observed a short regression during a hot-prefix migration. a few tenants saw increased soft-evictions and transient 429s for ~3 minutes. probable cause: overlapping grace windows + prefetch not reaching warm state on target.

sam: can you paste the logs/metrics you saw?

maya: sure. eviction_rate on node-7 spiked ~3x, token read tail latency increased ~120ms. logs:

maya: ```
W 10:14:05 demote: prefix=pref_hot_21 action=soft-evict reason=grace-timeout shard=7
I 10:14:06 prefetch: miss prefix=pref_hot_21 route=cold-read
W 10:14:07 demote: tombstone-compact scan=small duration=30ms prefix=pref_hot_21
```

li: is this the migration that did claim->demote->claim on the target without a warm-ack?

maya: yes. migration assumed prefetch would fill quickly. because we didn't extend the source grace window there was a period where both nodes considered the prefix evictable. tombstone cleanup freed meta the prefetch path expected, causing reads to fall back to cold-store.

nate: that double-evict style race is nasty, especially with compaction. were these soft or hard evicts?

maya: soft-evict, but compaction still ran. demote path checks lease epoch + residency; timing gap allowed compaction to remove small tombstones.

priya: can we link lease-claim metrics to eviction spikes? would help confirm handoff causality.

maya: pushed a quick grafana panel: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/evict-handoff — you can see lease_claims/sec aligned with eviction_rate.

sam: immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily lengthen grace window during migration, 2) add a short prefill_ack handshake before finalizing handoff.

li: caution: increasing grace increases memory pressure if a node holds many hot prefixes. make extension adaptive using hot_score + slab_pressure thresholds.

nate: alternative approach: introduce an in-flight handoff token. target claims but waits to demote source until target emits `prefill_ack` or a timeout occurs. makes handshake idempotent.

maya: we tried a prototype earlier (`handoff_token` + `prefill_ack`) — works but needs a safe fallback if prefill fails (e.g., OOM). current fallback re-claims source which causes churn.

priya: propose a backoff: target attempts prefill up to N times; if fails, serve reads from source (cooperative read-through) and mark a soft preference. only reassign if target eventually warms.

sam: add metrics: `handoff_latency`, `prefill_attempts`, `prefill_success_rate`, `handoff_failures`.

maya: short-term rollout plan:
- today: feature-flagged 30s grace extension during migration and halt migrations when prefetch rate > threshold. enable on canary nodes.
- 48h: implement `prefill_ack` handshake and emit events `handoff_start`, `prefill_ack`, `handoff_success`, `handoff_fail`.
- medium: fully idempotent handoff token + adaptive grace logic driven by hot_score and slab_pressure.

li: can the 30s bump be behind a FF scoped to canary?

maya: yes — created `ff.hot_pref_migration_grace` and enabled for canary only.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: ops/maya/hot-pref-grace -> canary-fleet. plan: rolling update 3 nodes at a time.

nate: another low-risk fix: make tombstone compaction lease-aware. if a prefix has recent handoff events, delay compacting its tiny tombstones by a short window (15-45s). cheap and prevents churn.

priya: agree. add config `tombstone_compaction_handoff_delay` default 0, set to 30s for canary.

sam: can we define a smoke test? steps: 1) generate hot traffic to prefix, 2) trigger migration, 3) assert no >5% increase in 429s and `prefill_ack` received within 60s.

maya: writing a smoke script. pseudocode:

maya: ```bash
# warm prefix
wrk -t4 -c80 -d45s http://canary/pref/pref_hot_21/generate
# trigger migration
curl -XPOST http://orchestrator/migrate -d '{"prefix":"pref_hot_21","target":"node-7"}'
# poll for events
curl http://eventstore/api/query?prefix=pref_hot_21 | jq .
```

li: add assertions for `prefill_ack` and tombstone_compaction_delay > 0. capture heap/compaction logs too.

nate: when you run, also capture slab pressure and free memory so we can validate adaptive grace heuristics later.

maya: will run and post results. initial canary run: small spike but `prefill_ack` succeeded and tombstone compaction was delayed; no sustained 429s.

sam: thanks. next steps: roll RFC for idempotent handoff token + prefill_ack with interface, invariants, and rollback semantics. include smoke test baseline and metrics.

priya: +1 for RFC. include the decision to keep tombstone delay configurable and the adaptive grace heuristic proposal in appendix.

maya: filing RFC after we validate canary metrics. I'll post the detailed run results here in ~30m. :thumbsup:
